absent: Locking, reference counting and lifetime rules for algorithm lists and transform instances.
Registration, lookup, allocation and destruction flows for crypto algorithms beyond inline helpers.
Numeric values and meanings of record signatures, revisions, severities and memory validity bits referenced but not defined here.
Privilege, ordering and concurrency requirements for MSR and port accesses on the companion chipset.
Timer allocation, register programming sequences and interrupt routing for MFGPT beyond the setup and release wrappers.
DAX device lifecycle, holder attachment and error handling beyond operation signatures, and PCIe capability and AER byte meanings.

findings.text: Record header describes a common error record envelope with leading signature area, revision and terminator marker, counts and severity, validation and length, timestamp, four platform and notification identifiers, record identity, flags, persistence info and trailing reserved space required to stay zero.

Section descriptor locates one body inside a record by byte offset and length and carries its own revision, small validation and flags fields, type and FRU identifiers, severity and short FRU text, with one reserved byte fixed to zero.

Generic processor section carries validation bits plus type, ISA, error type, operation, flags and level bytes, followed by version, brand string, processor, target, requestor and responder identities and instruction pointer.

Intel processor sections split identity, error detail and register context: one fixed part holds validation, APIC identity and CPU identity bytes; one error entry holds error type identifier with validation, check data and target, requestor, responder and pointer values; one context entry holds register type, array size, MSR address and memory register address.

ARM processor section records validation, counts of error and context entries, total length, affinity level with reserved padding, multiprocessor and model identifiers and running plus power state words. Each error entry carries version, length, validation, type, multiplicity, flags, packed error word and virtual and physical fault addresses. Each context entry carries version, type and size.

Memory error sections share topology and addressing detail: validation, status, address and mask, node through bit position hierarchy, requestor, responder and target identities and error type. The newer fixed form adds extended flag, rank and card and module handles. A compact form keeps only validation, topology, identities, rank, handles and extended flag without status, address and type.

PCI Express section combines validation and port type with a version tuple, command and status, device identity tuple of vendor, device, class, function, device number, segment, buses and slot, serial number halves, bridge status and control, plus fixed capability and AER areas.
Firmware error reference section is a small fixed header with record type, revision, padding, numeric identifier and GUID identifier.

ARM error reporting uses low flag bits for first, last, propagated and overflow, a small masked field for cache, TLB, bus and vendor categories, twelve validity indicators for transaction, operation, level, context corruption, corrected, precise and restartable program counter, participation, timeout, address space, memory attributes and access mode, and packed shift plus width pairs that locate each attribute inside a wide error word from bit sixteen through bit forty three.

Record and section headers impose fixed expectations: signature areas must match defined record and end markers, revision fields must match defined record revision, and stated reserved bytes must remain zero. Descriptor offsets are interpreted relative to the record header base, and ARM counts state how many error and context entries follow.

Memory extension helper exposes the extra row bits only when the row extension validity indicator is present; otherwise it reports no extension. When present it extracts the masked row portion from the extended byte and positions it at its defined shift.

Cipher family identifiers share a low nibble selector with distinct small values for cipher, authenticated encryption, light and synchronous ciphers, asymmetric cipher, signature, key exchange, asynchronous and synchronous compression, random, and hash families where hash and synchronous hash coincide and asynchronous hash uses the top nibble value; a companion mask isolates the asynchronous compression group.

Algorithm state and capability flags occupy single bits from bit four upward, distinguishing larval, dead, dying and asynchronous states, fallback need and prohibition, duplicate preference, tested, instance, kernel driver only, internal, optional key, no load, memory allocation, internal FIPS handling and virtual address request requirements.

Transform and request control uses a low bit for key needed, a mid mask covering request options, and single option bits that forbid weak keys and allow sleeping, backlog queueing and stack residence.

Algorithm names are bounded to one hundred twenty eight characters. Minimum crypto alignment follows the allocator minimum and is applied as an alignment attribute to algorithm and transform context storage.
Asynchronous completion is reported through a callback receiving the originating request pointer and a status code, allowing upper layers to associate completion data with the request object.
Async request header links queue membership with completion callback, opaque data, owning transform pointer and request flags.

Single block cipher description states minimum and maximum key sizes and provides key setup plus single block encryption and decryption operations; the generic algorithm union reaches this description through a cipher accessor name.

Algorithm descriptor links global and user lists, holds flags, block, context, alignment and request sizes, priority and reference count, generic and driver names, type pointer, a union currently carrying the cipher description, init, exit and destroy operations and owning module, with whole descriptor aligned to crypto minimum.
Synchronous wait helper pairs a completion primitive with a status field; a declaration helper creates an on stack instance with completion initialized and status cleared.

Wait helpers convert deferred crypto outcomes into blocking waits: progress and busy indications cause a wait for completion followed by rearming and reporting of the stored status, while other statuses pass through unchanged; a separate initializer prepares the completion for reuse.

Synchronous crypto use moves from initialized wait through submitted request to either immediate result or blocked wait; on wakeup the stored completion status becomes the call result and the completion is rearmed for a later submission.
Transform instance holds flags, allocation node, fallback transform pointer, exit operation, back pointer to its algorithm and trailing aligned context storage.

Transform helpers expose algorithm identity and geometry by forwarding to the owning algorithm descriptor, manipulate flag bits by set and clear, report context alignment and asynchronous capability from algorithm flags, and release a transform by delegating to the generic destroy path with the transform as its own namespace argument.

Request helpers report stack residence from flags, install callback, data and option flags while preserving stack residence, bind a transform while clearing stack residence, and initialize a stack request by clearing flags, binding the transform and then marking stack residence.

Stack residence is sticky across callback updates but not across transform binding: callback installation keeps the existing stack mark and applies only non sticky option bits, transform binding always clears the mark, and stack initialization reasserts it after binding.

Geode companion MSR numbers identify a GLIU window, LX and GX global configuration and pad selects, graphics clock PLLs, local bus enables for SMB, GPIO, MFGPT, ACPI and power management, soft reset, PIC Y and Z selects and LPC mask, MFGPT interrupt, count and setup, RTC day, month and century offsets, and an LX spare register.

PIC Z high selector updates one four bit group field inside the shared register by read, masked clear of the group nibble, masked insert of the low interrupt nibble and write back, always reporting success.

CS5536 board constants fix two PIC select ports, four local bus window sizes for GPIO, MFGPT, ACPI and power management, power management register offsets for clocks, sleep, wake data and status, enable and control groups for fixed and general events, single bit wake, RTC and power button indicators duplicated in status and enable views, and high bit PME flags and enables for two GPIO lines.

Virtual System Architecture access uses a paired index and data port with an unlock value, plus register numbers for signature and memory size and two accepted signature values distinguishing vendor variants.

VSA presence probe unlocks the virtual register interface, selects the signature register and compares the returned value against the two known signatures, caching the boolean outcome across calls so later queries avoid hardware access.

GPIO register map fixes offsets for output value, enable, open drain, invert and auxiliary selects, pull up and down, input enable, invert, filter, event count, read back and auxiliary input, events enable and lock, positive and negative edge enables and statuses, a filter amount, four map registers and a function select.

Multi function timer constants bound the timer count with a wildcard selector, distinguish working, standby and combined power domains, number two comparators, encode interrupt, NMI and reset event actions, index comparator, counter and setup registers, and define single setup bits for counting, comparator enables, setup mode, stop, external and reverse enables and clock select.
MFGPT interrupt helpers are thin wrappers that forward timer, comparator and interrupt arguments to a common setter with an enable or disable indication for setup versus release.

Direct access storage uses an unsigned entry type, a two state access mode distinguishing normal access from recovery write, an operations table for address translation with page run length plus zeroing and poison recovery write, and a holder table for memory failure notification with offset, length and flags.
Four headers protect against multiple inclusion with a single defining macro each for crypto, CS5535 companion, DASD module and DAX interfaces.

Callers must honor alignment and lifetime risks: reserved CPER bytes must stay zero or parsers may reject records, MSR and port operations act on global hardware without visible locking, VSA probing caches its first result so later hardware changes are invisible, crypto completions must be initialized and rearmed before reuse, and stack request flags must be set only for genuinely stack resident objects.
